reuse.why: Reuses findOrCreateBank, syncAccount, handleSyncResponse, getServer/post and one shared link guard across all providers, but the takeover rewrites unlinkAccount's field reset instead of sharing it, and Fintegra linking/downloading are fresh copies of the Akahu code.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near-verbatim copy of linkAkahuAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions, the Fintegra starting-balance branch is identical to the Akahu branch, and the unlink column reset is copied from unlinkAccount.

placement.why: Guards sit beside the link handlers in accounts/app.ts, the download and balance logic in sync.ts, the URL in server-config and the type in types/models, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the four requested behaviours and their tests; nothing unrelated is touched.

maintainability.why: The link rules are centralised, but a check-named helper (ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked) now also unlinks another account behind a boolean flag, and adding Fintegra grows the per-provider copy surface by three more blocks.

bypasses_abstraction.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked in server/accounts/app.ts clears account_id/bank/balances/sync_source/status with its own db.updateAccount instead of sharing the reset that unlinkAccount ('account-unlink') already performs.

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (linkFintegraAccount vs linkAkahuAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions vs downloadAkahuTransactions, the fintegra balance branch in processBankSyncDownload, the unlink reset) are open, near-verbatim copies rather than disguised ones.

abstraction_drift.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked gained the replaceExistingLink parameter and a branch that unlinks the holding account inside what was a pure guard; all six provider link functions, Fintegra included, still call it.
